name: Amazon Q
oneLiner: Named-user seats billed monthly whether anyone uses them, plus index units billed by the hour.
trap: Q Business index units bill hourly regardless of query volume, on top of seats you pay for even for dormant users. Q in Connect adds per-message and per-voice-minute charges.

name: Amazon Athena
oneLiner: You pay for the bytes your query reads off S3 - the number of queries barely matters.
trap: Bytes scanned drives the bill, not query count. Partitioning and Parquet/ORC are the lever. DDL and failed queries are free; cancelled queries still bill for what they scanned.

name: Amazon Bedrock
oneLiner: On-demand is per input and output token; Provisioned Throughput is an hourly rental of model units.
trap: Provisioned Throughput bills per model unit per hour whether you invoke it or not, on a 1- or 6-month commit. Cache-read and cache-write tokens bill separately from input/output.

name: Amazon CloudSearch
oneLiner: Closed to new customers; instances bill hourly and index rebuilds bill per GB stored.
trap: An IndexDocuments request you trigger yourself is charged against the full size of data already in the domain, so schema tweaks on a big domain hurt. Rebuilds AWS initiates on its own are not charged.

name: Amazon Comprehend
oneLiner: Per 100-character unit of text, minimum 3 units a request - unless you run a custom endpoint.
trap: Custom sync endpoints bill per inference unit from the moment you start them until you delete them, even with zero documents analyzed. Tiny requests still round up to 300 characters.

name: Amazon Elastic Transcoder
oneLiner: Gone since November 13, 2025; MediaConvert is the replacement.
trap: AWS discontinued the service on November 13, 2025 and console access went with it. Billing was per minute of output, rounded up to a whole minute per file, SD at half the HD rate, failed transcodes usually free.

name: Amazon EMR
oneLiner: An EMR surcharge on top of the EC2 bill, per second, for every node - running or completely idle.
trap: The classic disaster is a cluster left up after the job finished. EMR bills from cluster-ready until you shut it down regardless of work, and EC2 plus EBS are charged separately.

name: Amazon Forecast
oneLiner: Closed to new signups; existing users pay per GB imported, per training hour, per thousand data points.
trap: Data points multiply fast. A predictor emits a point for every quantile at every step of the horizon across all series, and explanations multiply that again by the number of attributes explained.

name: Amazon Fraud Detector
oneLiner: Predictions are cheap per call; the deployed model holds the meter open.
trap: Billed training compute hours can exceed elapsed training time, because Fraud Detector picks bigger instances than the baseline spec. A deployed model then bills hourly for hosting until you undeploy it.

name: AWS Glue
oneLiner: Jobs and crawlers bill by DPU-second while they run; the Data Catalog bills for objects and lookups.
trap: Crawlers carry a 10-minute minimum per run, so a 5-minute crawl schedule bills nonstop. Over-provisioned DPUs cost the same whether Spark actually uses them or not.

name: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
oneLiner: You pay per labeled object, twice over.
trap: Two charges land per object: the Ground Truth service fee and the workforce fee. Mechanical Turk tasks price per worker, so raising workers-per-object for label quality multiplies the human half.

name: AWS IoT Analytics
oneLiner: Support ended on December 15, 2025.
trap: While it ran, the same data got metered three ways: per GB through the pipeline, per TB scanned by dataset SQL, and per GB-month for the raw and processed copies kept side by side. Console and resources are gone now.

name: Amazon Interactive Video Service (IVS)
oneLiner: Input hours and viewer output hours, both by the hour; chat adds a per-message charge.
trap: Input hours accrue for as long as you push video at a channel, with zero viewers watching. Output hours are a separate meter that scales with audience, so a test stream left broadcasting overnight still bills.

name: Amazon Kendra
oneLiner: An empty index costs exactly what a busy one costs.
trap: AWS states it plainly: once an index exists you pay for it with zero documents and zero queries, and deleting it is the only way to stop the meter. Kendra also closes to new customers on July 30, 2026.

name: AWS Lake Formation
oneLiner: Lake Formation permissions and LF-Tags cost nothing - every dollar lands on the services underneath.
trap: Being free makes people forget where the bill moved: Glue Data Catalog, crawlers, S3, and the Athena/EMR/Redshift scans it governs all charge normally.

name: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
oneLiner: You rent KPUs by the second for as long as the application is RUNNING - traffic or no traffic.
trap: A running app processing zero events still bills a 2-KPU minimum plus storage (Studio: 3 KPUs), and every app pays one extra orchestration KPU. Stop apps, do not just drain them.

name: AWS Elemental MediaConvert
oneLiner: Per minute of output, times a multiplier for every codec, resolution and feature you turn on.
trap: Billing counts output minutes rather than source minutes. A 10-minute mezzanine encoded into a six-rung ABR ladder bills 60 minutes, and each rung applies its own resolution and frame-rate multiplier.

name: AWS Elemental MediaLive
oneLiner: Every input and output bills by the hour.
trap: Stopping a channel does not take it to zero. MediaLive has an explicit idle-channel charge for stopped channels and an idle charge for push inputs; only pull inputs are free while idle. Delete to stop paying.

name: AWS Elemental MediaPackage
oneLiner: Two per-GB meters: what goes in, and what gets packaged back out.
trap: Ingest is metered per GB too, so a high-bitrate contribution feed costs money before a single viewer connects. Origination falls off sharply once a CDN caches segments, which is why AWS pushes CloudFront.

name: AWS Elemental MediaTailor
oneLiner: Ad insertions bill per thousand, but a Channel Assembly channel bills every hour it runs.
trap: Two products share one bill. Ad insertion meters per thousand insertions, while Channel Assembly meters per running channel hour, so a linear channel with no audience still accrues hours. Ad delivery is per GB.

name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
oneLiner: A cluster you rent by the hour plus the disk under it; the searches themselves are free.
trap: Nodes bill 24/7 whether anyone searches or not, and Serverless collections hold an OCU floor. Transfer out of the domain is charged; node-to-node inside it is not.

name: Amazon Personalize
oneLiner: Ingest bills per GB, training bills per hour, recommendations bill per thousand.
trap: Custom solutions only cost you when you train or ask for recommendations. Use-case optimized recommenders behave differently: each active recommender carries an hourly rate that keeps running with no traffic.

name: Amazon Polly
oneLiner: Per character of text you synthesize; generative and long-form voices cost far more per character.
trap: Speech Marks bill at the same per-character rate as audio, so asking for both doubles it. Cache the audio - replay is free, re-synthesizing the identical string is not.

name: Amazon QuickSight
oneLiner: Authors pay a flat monthly seat whether they log in or not; readers can be billed per 30-minute session.
trap: Author seats bill monthly even when unused, and SPICE is GB-month on top. Reader sessions are 30-minute blocks with a per-user monthly cap - model seats vs sessions before choosing.

name: Amazon Rekognition
oneLiner: Per image for stills, per minute for video - but custom models bill by the hour while hosted.
trap: Custom Labels bills per inference hour while the model is running: you keep being charged even if no images are processed. Stored face metadata also bills every month.

name: Amazon SageMaker AI
oneLiner: Training stops billing when the job ends; a real-time endpoint bills until you delete it.
trap: Endpoints charge per instance-hour from creation to deletion with zero invocations - the top SageMaker surprise. Use serverless or async scale-to-zero for bursty traffic.

name: Amazon Textract
oneLiner: Per page, per feature - stacking Forms, Tables and Queries on one page multiplies that page's price.
trap: Cost scales with pages and with how many features you ask for per page, not with API calls. A 200-page PDF is 200 billable pages, and re-processing it bills again - there is no caching.

name: Amazon Transcribe
oneLiner: Per second of audio you feed it, with a 15-second floor on every single request.
trap: Billing follows audio duration, not request count, and each request rounds up to 15 seconds - chopping a stream into tiny clips inflates the bill. Call Analytics is priced separately.

name: Amazon Translate
oneLiner: Per character of source text, whitespace included - Active Custom Translation costs much more.
trap: Whitespace counts as billable characters and re-translating unchanged strings bills again, so cache output. Active Custom Translation is several times the standard per-character rate.
